findings.title: Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud Security Incident (N-able Uptime event 202672)
findings.summary_md: N-able's status page says a disruption first reported on November 16 was caused by a security incident involving unauthorized access to one server in the Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud environment. The company says it disabled UI and API access proactively while mail flow and spam filtering continued, and that it had no evidence at that time of customer data or tenant mailbox compromise. N-able states that this incident is unrelated to the N-central incident.

findings.title: N-able Confirmed Unauthorized Access to One Mail Assure Server. Here's What to Ask Your Provider.
findings.summary_md: Brotherly Technology reports that the disruption began at 10:00 p.m. ET on November 16 and was first attributed to platform configuration and service dependencies. It records N-able reclassifying the event as a security incident at 10:05 p.m. ET on November 17, with mail flow and filtering still operating and no evidence of customer data or mailbox access. As of 7:56 a.m. ET on November 18, the dashboard, quarantine, logging and mailbox synchronization were still being restored, and the article advises MSP customers to ask about quarantined mail and credential rotation.
